reviews.review: When Giant Ants and Spiders come out to play you don't use bug spray, you use a mega ton bomb.

Earth Defense Force 5 is an absolute blast from start to finish. Lemme set this up for you. Try to imagine War of the Worlds...but if it was made in Japan. Even then that's not a proper way to describe this game. 

**PROS**
1: Multiplayer. Cannot stress enough the pure CHAOS that is Multiplayer. The game on Solo is chaotic enough but combine that with friends? Who are possibly just as trigger happy as you are and run the risk of TPKing everything with one misplaced shot of a Splash Grenade or a Missile Launch? Makes for some hilarious fun.

2: Ragdoll Physics. Because every game needs these. Imagine blowing up a cluster of Ants with a Hunter Cruise Missile and sending all their bits, and yourself, walking in the air like you're in The Snowman Music Video.

3: The Classes. Not a one of these is bad. All are dumb fun. From the Simple Ranger to the Iron Man's Older Cousin, Fencer, To the High Speed High Flying High EXPLOSIVE Wing Diver, To the Doritos Munching, Monster Energy Drink Guzzlin Air Raider, none of these classes are lacking in diversity and fun. You can take a shotgun to an Alien's Face or Literally Smite Them with a Laser Beam From God (Aka A Satellite), Blow them up with a Bombing Run of Missiles, snipe a Frog's head off with a Railgun Sniper or Just Laser Lightshow them to death. Just pick a class and have fun.

4: The Weapons. Shotguns, Rifles, Snipers, Missiles, Rockets, Bombs, Grenades, Lasers, Lances, Hammers, Swords which I affectionately call the Can Openers, Flamethrowers, Miniguns, Space Lasers, Mini Lasers, The Room Clearing Stardust Cannon, Airships, Tanks, Helicopters, BIGGER Tanks, A &#^*!ING PACIFIC RIM/GUNDAM MECH SUIT! If it exists you'd probably find it here, ready for some Warhammer 40K style Dakka Making.

5: The Story. It is Hilariously Bad in some places, Surprisingly good in others. Like seriously some of the voice acting and story elements in this game will want you to facepalm your skull in but on the other hand, it's endearingly daft and charming. It's like this game's Script was ripped straight out of a B-Movie from the Golden Age of Hollywood era. And I find that charming, even if I wanna scream "YOU &^#&ING MORONS!" when the EDF is made out as the Idiots because they need the Primary Protags to do it first before they realize "OH! That's what we need to do!" Overall I'd give it a 6 out of 10. It's cringe worthy and daft in some areas. But in others it's charming in it's Daftness. And in some places when you look past the cheese, this game gets INCREDIBLY Dark. 

**CONS**
1: The Story. As I said it's endearingly daft. But the parts that are bad are just...unnnnngh...From the EDF not realizing until 5 IN GAME MONTHS LATER to hit the Teleportation Ships in the GLOWING RED WEAKSPOT when the Ships open up to drop monsters in, to them calling Giant Frog People 'Similar to Humans' which...THEY CLEARLY ARE NOT, to straight up not calling the Monsters what they clearly are. (Occasionally they do but this is sparingly). Like they classify Species Alpha and Species Beta early on in the game. Wanna know what Species Alpha and Beta are? GIANT BLACK ANTS and GIANT SPIDERS that look like Lucas The Spider's Murderous Cousins from Outer Space. JUST CALL EM WHAT THEY ARE! Sheesh.

2: The GRIND. Oooooof...Just so much grinding. Ok this is how the system works. In EDF 5 you don't gradually unlock stuff as you progress through the story. You unlock them by zooming around and collecting these Crates that drop from enemies when you kill them. Red Crates give Armor which is your Health. More Armor means more Health and it's crucial for survival. Green Crates give Weapons. Ya know, The Good Stuff. Small White and Large White Crates restore your health if you take damage during a mission. (Trust me YOU WILL Take damage at some point no matter what mission.) So you go around collecting these crates to unlock better and better stuff and get more and more health. Sounds pretty good right? Well yeah. Until you realize that any weapons you pick up can be either Weapons you already have or weapons for a class you don't wanna play right now. Or ever will play if you don't like the class. (Which is Understandable, Fencer is a complex class or Ranger may be too simple for some.) Now getting the same weapons you already have is not a bad thing. These weapons can be better upgraded versions of the weapons you already have. Replacing the lesser version and getting a stronger version. Especially useful when you have a particular weapon you really like. But then you may get the same weapon that is inferior in every way and ends up just being a Dud weapon. The Positive is, unlike previous entries, you don't get stuff exclusive to the class you play. You get a mishmash of stuff for all classes, Weapons and Armor both. So even if you don't play other classes, you still get stuff for those other classes so when you do play them ya still have some goodies to play with. Now repeat this process. Not only for higher difficulties but also on EVERY. SINGLE. ONE. Of the +100 Missions in this game. Yeah. Be prepared to sink HOURS into this game just to get stuff you NEED For the higher difficulties and tougher missions. And speaking of difficulties...

3: The Difficulty. Oh Jesus Wept a Bloody River, the Difficulty. You have 5 Difficulty Levels. 3 of which are already unlocked by Default. Easy, Normal and Hard. 2 of which you unlock after you beat the Campaign once. Hardest and Inferno. Now in my experience, Hard Difficulty on Solo is kinda not bad at all really. Sure the enemies are tougher and deal more damage the higher you go but on Solo it's pretty manageable. The Higher the Difficulty, The Better Gear and Armor you get. As per expectations. And Hard Solo is not too tough. BUT! The issues arise when you play Multiplayer. On Solo the reason it isn't so bad is because the game tweaks the toughness of the enemies in accordance with the mode you play. Solo Hard? Manageable. Multiplayer Hard? *PTSD Noises* Oh and there's also a Level Cap! When you get Badass weaponry you wanna use, you can use em on Solo with Free Reign. But on Multiplayer, depending on the Difficulty and Mission, you are limited in the level of equipment and amount of armor you can take with you. Granted you can remove this but only when you have at least an 80% Completion Rate. But this PALES in comparison to INFERNO Difficulty. You will cry blood and spit lava you're so freaking traumatized from how tough it is. It makes Dark Souls look EASY. And that's just Solo. Multiplayer Inferno? Even Doom Slayer would be waving the white flag. So I hope you have plenty of Tylonal. Because you're gonna be getting Migranes from the difficulty. Oh! And you know the funny part? If you're a Completionist? Ya gotta play. Inferno Difficulty. ON EVERY. SINGLE. CLASS. AND YOU GOTTA BEAT AT LEAST SOME INFERNO DIFFICULTY MISSIONS TO REACH THAT 80% COMPLETION RATE I MENTIONED TO UNLOCK THE LEVEL CAPS IN MULTIPLAYER! **AND** the Multiplayer and Solo campaigns are separate! What do I mean by that? Well if you complete a mission on Solo, it doesn't count as being completed in Multiplayer. Which means, ya gotta beat both Solo and Multiplayer Campaigns for a 100% COMPLETION RATE! AHAHAHAHAHAHAHAAAAAAH!

*Takes a Deeeeeeep Breath*

In conclusion, This game is an exercise in madness. It will make you rage. Cry. Bleed even (I should see a doctor). But. When you don't care for completion, you just wanna play some missions with your buds, When you turn your brain off, And just have fun, There is no other game in the world that can capture that Childlike Glee of just Nuking everything in a straight line or Blasting a Laser from Space to bifurcate some poor alien, or watching as your ally drops a cruise missile in point blank range and watch as their body goes flying from one side of the map to the other along with several dozens of parts of monsters and baptizing yourself (and the map) in a tsunami of multicolored blood.

Enemies drop 3 different items: Green(weapons), Red(armor=health), White(healing, large and small - self-explanatory). Red armor can be collected an unlimited number of times; each red chest gives one armor point (health) and can be stacked indefinitely. After completing a map, you receive your loot (weapons and armor). Each difficulty level increases the quality of the weapons found in the chests. Each map has its own special weapon drops. Weapons obtained twice improve (merge) the original weapon. New players should start the game on Normal difficulty. Higher difficulty levels are unlocked gradually. The goal is to play on Inferno difficulty to obtain the highest quality weapons, but this requires very strong equipment and a lot of armor. The enemies on Inferno are extremely strong and have a lot of health. (Single-player and multiplayer are separate. What you earn in single-player is not available in multiplayer.) New enemy types are introduced every few levels. The game starts very easy and gets progressively harder. Please never pull everyone at once unless you know what you're doing. The basic requirements for having fun here are not to take the game too seriously and just enjoy yourself.
